title: Lexicographically Smallest String After a Swap
summary: Given a string s consisting solely of digits, provide the lexicographically smallest string achievable by swapping adjacent digits with the same parity at most once.
statement: Given a string s consisting solely of digits, provide the lexicographically smallest string achievable by swapping adjacent digits with the same parity at most once. Digits are of the same parity if both are odd or both are even.
constraints: You may perform at most one swap of adjacent decimal digits.
The two swapped digits must have the same parity.
Return the lexicographically smallest obtainable string.
hints: A beneficial swap must be a same-parity adjacent descent.
The earliest changed position dominates all later lexicographic effects.
Scan left to right and swap the first allowed descent, then stop.
Any later swap leaves this earliest improvable digit larger, while a non-descent cannot improve the string.
editorial: Any later swap leaves this earliest improvable digit larger, while a non-descent cannot improve the string.

tests.explanation: The first useful same-parity descent is 5,3; swapping it produces 43520.
No allowed adjacent swap makes the string smaller.
